title: County of Champagne
capsule: The County of Champagne emerged as a powerful feudal principality in northeastern France around 990 under the House of Blois-Champagne, reaching its apogee in the twelfth and thirteenth centuries under Counts Henry I (r. 1152–1181) and Thibaut IV (r. 1201–1253). Its greatest distinction was the Champagne Fairs—six annual cycles at Troyes, Provins, Lagny, and Bar-sur-Aube—that made the county the financial and commercial crossroads of northern Europe, linking Flemish cloth merchants with Italian bankers. Thibaut IV's granddaughter Joan inherited the county; her 1284 marriage to the future Philip IV of France brought Champagne into the French royal domain, confirmed by Philip's accession in 1285.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Boundaries are well attested through medieval cartography, charters, and administrative records; the county's extent is among the better-documented of high-medieval French principalities.
